The land in the vicinity of the proposed project is currently in a transitional period from agricultural to residential, commercial and light industrial use. With this new development much of the surface of the land has already been altered due to fill areas and cut or borrow areas. The areas in the vicinity of I-94 and along Howell Avenue and west of General Mitchell Field are already disturbed areas. Very little of the landscape remains unaltered.
On site investigations show that the intermittant streams between I-94 and General Mitchell Field are not in their natural state and have been altered by incorporation into the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage Commission man-made drainage ditch system.
Woodland resources have already been diminished by the urbanization process. Original vegetation is gone and the land is covered now by grasses and weeds. Some trees such as American Elm, Cedar and Poplar remain. Since the vegetation is sparse and the surrounding area is undergoing development, wildlife is also limited. The Department of Natural Resources has indicated that there will be no significant impact on fish or wildlife habitat and that there are no known rare or endangered species in the area.
